title: Quantum Entanglement: Non-Local Correlations
text:
Quantum entanglement is a physical phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same existence, regardless of the physical distance separating them. The state of one particle instantaneously influences the measurable properties of the other particle(s), a correlation that Einstein famously dubbed "spooky action at a distance."

The connection described by entanglement is not based on classical variables or hidden local instructions. Instead, it implies a shared quantum wave function describing the entire system. Measurement of an observable (such as spin or polarization) on one entangled particle collapses the combined wave function, immediately fixing the corresponding value for the other particles simultaneously.

This non-local correlation has profound implications for physics and technology. It forms the theoretical backbone for emerging fields such as quantum computing, where entangled qubits could perform calculations far beyond the capability of classical bits, and quantum cryptography, enabling perfectly secure communication channels.
